label: Game B
nuance_found: Chained mirror relay: aim mirror 1 so it lights mirror 2, which lights mirror 3 on a ledge you have to hang and climb to reach, then aim each last mirror at a dark stela; a stone block sat in the beam and had to be pulled clear. Level 2 introduces warden stamp plates with a ring you must step out of, which I saw but did not solve. It is a real puzzle with interacting parts, but there is no score, no time pressure and nothing to optimise.
audio: Procedural wind and drone ambience with swelling chords, noise bursts for light and doors, a low thud when blocks move; no real music track and no punchy hit sounds.
furthest_progress: Cleared level 1 The Sunken Court (all 3 stelae lit, far door opened at about 448 s) and entered level 2 The Checkpoint; read the clerk, took Mira's sun disc, stood on the crescent plate, 0 of 3 plates stamped.
used_movement_assist: yes, about 45 times (goto to mirrors, objective, plates)
control_trouble: Turning a mirror needs Use held plus the stick, which a real thumb pair does easily; my two-finger bursts kept walking me off the mirror and the aim took about 90 acts. Most of that is the harness, not the game.
best_moment: Third stela lights and the gate opens onto a glowing ringed planet, then the level title card.
worst_moment: The screen cut to black about five times when I pulled the block or stepped away from a mirror (camera inside geometry), and the first level took about 450 s with no scoring hook.
verdict: It looks gorgeous and the mirror relay is a real puzzle, but I am a score chaser and this gave me nothing to chase: no points, no timer, no combo, just a long fiddly aiming job while a camera that blacks out on me. The first stela took me about 200 s and the gate about 450 s, which is miles too slow for me. If I liked slow puzzle games I would keep it, but I would delete it after a day.
